Prototype · #541 · for the owner's review

Talked about now: the start page row

Five variants of the row (E added after the owner picked D), at the top of the real section below the living room, on the real room as a guest sees it. Real titles in the news in the week of 14 October 2026 with their TMDB posters; the reasons follow the week's news, the numbers, curves, posts and headlines are made up. Nothing is fetched from a third party.

Run it

cd goodwatch-webapp   # a worktree without .env
npm ci && npx patch-package
__VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS=alp-laptop.tail3b99f1.ts.net \
REC_TASTE_MATCH=on REC_FILTER_BAR=on REC_WATCH_NEXT=on REC_TASTE_PAGE=on REC_EXPLORER=on \
REC_NAVIGATION=on REC_AGE_FILTER=on REC_TRACKING=on \
npx remix vite:dev --port 3151 --strictPort --host 100.71.215.115

Then open http://alp-laptop.tail3b99f1.ts.net:3151/prototype/start-row?variant=E#browse and switch with the floating bar or ← → (A to E). The #browse opens the page below the room, as “More below” does.

Recommendation

Update, after the owner's pick: D was chosen, with more of B's native content in it; that is E. Build E, with two guards: the lead shows only the pieces it has (no empty slots), and rows without any content keep D's two lines. C's lip line still works on top of it, so the room's first screen names the top three.

The first recommendation, before the pick: ship A, with C's lip line, and keep the talk itself for the title page. A works on the buzz score and a reason alone, so it can launch before the content flows are good, it needs no consent on the start page, and it stays cacheable and light. The lip line (C) is the only thing that reaches the room's first screen and costs one line of text. B is the right shape for a title page's section, where one title's content is enough to fill it; on the start page it needs good content for seven titles every day. From D, take the “×N its usual” figure into A's fact line if the score flow stores daily history; the full board is a later experiment.

A · RankedB · MixedC · TickerD · Pulse (own idea)E · Pulse + native (after the owner's pick of D)

ARanked

/prototype/start-row?variant=A#browse

Tests
Is a chart of titles enough? Ten posters with big outlined rank numbers, a reason chip (Trailer drop, Netflix Top 10, News spike, New series, Out Friday), one line of fact and the move since yesterday.
Tradeoffs
Needs only the buzz score and a reason per title, no third-party content and no consent; the cheapest to ship and it degrades well. It says why in two words but shows none of the talk itself; the rank numbers take width, so a phone sees two cards at a time.

BMixed

/prototype/start-row?variant=B#browse

Tests
Should the row carry the talk itself? Each hot title is followed by its trailer (click-to-load facade with our own TMDB picture), a post (Bluesky, Mastodon) and a headline, grouped under a rule with the rank.
Tradeoffs
The richest and the most alive, but every group needs good content every day, which is the hard half per the research; a title without any leaves a hole. It brings the consent facade, report links and the lawyer's questions (server-rendered post text) onto the start page. Long rail: about 25 cards for 7 titles.

CTicker

/prototype/start-row?variant=C#browse

Tests
Is a light touch enough? One crawling line (it stops under the pointer or focus; reduced motion makes it a strip to swipe), Expand opens the ten as a list. The room's lip says “Talked about now: East of Eden, Below, Avengers…”, so the first screen names them.
Tradeoffs
Smallest footprint and the only variant visible from the room's first screen (through the lip). A crawl is hard to read and to press, motion is a cost, and it looks like news, not like GoodWatch. The lip line works with any variant.

DPulse (own idea)

/prototype/start-row?variant=D#browse

Tests
Should GoodWatch show why a title is hot as data, as it does for scores and fingerprints? Each title has its 14-day buzz curve with the day of the reason marked and “×2.4 its usual”. One title is the lead (backdrop, full curve with a hover readout, its best piece of content); pressing a row makes it the lead. On a phone the lead opens in the board under its row.
Tradeoffs
The most distinctive and honest about the ranking, and the curve is free data (Wikipedia pageviews). It is dense, and “×2.1” next to rank 1 while rank 2 shows ×5.9 needs explaining (rank is volume, × is change). Needs daily history stored, and the lead makes the phone version long.

EPulse + native (after the owner's pick of D)

/prototype/start-row?variant=E#browse

Tests
D with B's native displays in it. The lead keeps D's curve and “×N its usual” and adds its two or three best pieces as they are on their platforms: the trailer behind the click-to-load facade, then a headline and a Bluesky or Mastodon post side by side (a strip to swipe on a phone). Each row of the board gets one line of preview: the platforms' marks and a post's first words (or a headline), so the board says what is being said before it is pressed.
Tradeoffs
Keeps D's honesty about the ranking and gets B's life without B's long rail: only the lead carries full content, so one good title a day is enough and a title with less shows less (rank 6 has no video, so its backdrop heads the lead). It still brings the consent facade and the lawyer's question (post text on our server) onto the start page, the rows grow a line, and the lead is now taller than the board on desktop.
